deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a finite arrangement of pseudo-lines in the projective plane, forming a 'carte' with 1-skeleton K^1. Each pseudo-line D carries an induced combinatorial polygon structure. Ω(D) is the two-element set of orientations of D. On the previous page Grothendieck notes that for a vertex s and a pseudo-line D not through s, the local orientations Ω_s(X) of the plane at s are in canonical bijection with Ω(D). The reason is that P^2 minus D is a disc containing s, and an orientation of that disc corresponds to an orientation of its boundary. The question he poses there is how to make the composite bijection Ω(D) ≅ Ω_s ≅ Ω(D') explicit, purely in terms of the combinatorics of K^1 and its pseudo-lines, when D and D' both avoid s. Let t = D ∩ D'.

This page answers it in steps.

(1) Basic case. Take two pseudo-lines Δ, Δ' through s that do not pass through t. Let u, u' be the intersections of Δ with D, D', and v, v' those of Δ' with D, D'. The four pseudo-lines D, D', Δ, Δ' are in general position. Four pseudo-lines in general position have a single combinatorial type, which is stretchable ('position standard'), so the question reduces to real projective geometry. There one checks that the orientation of D given by the arrow u→v corresponds to the orientation of D' given by u'→v'.

(2) General case. Let Δ_1, ..., Δ_k pass through s and not through t, meeting D in u_i and D' in u'_i. Give D−{t} and D'−{t} (combinatorial affine lines) the linear orders induced by corresponding orientations. If the Δ_i are numbered so that the u_i increase, then the u'_i increase as well. This is a combinatorial version of the perspectivity from s, which maps D to D' and fixes t. It describes the bijection Ω(D) ≅ Ω(D') combinatorially whenever at least two pseudo-lines pass through s and avoid t.

(3) Exceptional case. Only one pseudo-line Δ' passes through s and not through t. This forces s to have order 4: exactly two pseudo-lines pass through s, and the other one, Δ, passes through both s and t. He then looks for an auxiliary pseudo-line D'' not through s. The margin notes that such a D'' is automatically different from Δ and Δ'. What has to be excluded is that the whole figure reduces to a pencil through t plus one secant. Let x, x' be the points where D'' meets D, D', and u, u' the points where the relevant line meets D, D'. If x ≠ u and x' ≠ u', step (1)/(2) can be applied to compare Ω(D) with Ω(D'') and Ω(D'') with Ω(D'), and then compose.

The next page treats the remaining degenerate configurations: two pencils centred at t and u (or u'), and a fallback using two auxiliary pseudo-lines Γ, Γ'.

Overall aim: a purely combinatorial description of the orientation local system (the orientation double cover) of the projective plane, in terms of the cell structure of a pseudo-line arrangement. This feeds his programme on the combinatorial ('modérée') description of such arrangements.
errors: The appeal to 'general position, hence standard position' is legitimate for four pseudo-lines: there is only one simple arrangement type, and every arrangement of at most 8 pseudo-lines is stretchable.

For step (2) with k pseudo-lines, Grothendieck implicitly relies on the pencil-through-s plus D, D' configuration behaving like the straight case. This is fine, because the claim follows from the four-line case applied pairwise to consecutive Δ_i, Δ_j.
The case analysis is unfinished on this page: degenerate configurations (pencils) are deferred to the next page and are called 'demande encore un traitement à part'.
Well-definedness (independence of the choice of auxiliary lines) is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Orientation of a pseudo-line D is equivalent to a local orientation of the plane at any point off D. The comparison between two lines D, D' avoiding a vertex s is computed by perspectivity from s: the orders of the points cut out on D−{t} and D'−{t} by the lines through s correspond.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial description of the orientation double cover / orientation local system of RP^2 for a pseudo-line arrangement; closely related to the chirotope of a rank-3 oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence (1978) topological representation of oriented matroids; Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Bokowski, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (Oriented Matroids, 1993)
ideas.where_published: Not known in published Grothendieck texts; pseudo-line systems may be alluded to in the context of 'géométrie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme, but unsure

ideas.what: Four pseudo-lines in general position are 'en position standard', i.e. combinatorially equivalent to four real lines (a projective frame).
ideas.modern_name: Stretchability of small simple pseudo-line arrangements (all arrangements of ≤8 pseudo-lines are stretchable)

ideas.what: Reduction of the transport problem to auxiliary pseudo-lines D'' (and Γ, Γ' on the next page), with a case analysis of degenerate pencil configurations.
ideas.modern_name: Connectivity / case analysis in the arrangement graph

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks an intrinsic combinatorial description, in terms of the cell complex K^1 alone, of the canonical bijections Ω(D) ≅ Ω_s(X) ≅ Ω(D'), i.e. of the orientation local system of the projective plane. He gets it in the generic case via perspectivity and leaves the degenerate pencil configurations to a separate case analysis.
missed.quote: Cela décrit la bijection Ω(D) ≃ Ω(D') en termes de la combinatoire de K^1 et de ses pseudo-droites, sauf dans le cas où il n'y a qu'une seule ps-droite Δ' passant par s et non par t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially recovering chirotope/orientation data from the unoriented arrangement, which oriented-matroid theory already handles. It is an independent, sheaf-flavoured viewpoint (orientations as a local system on the cell complex), but it is unlikely to contain anything new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, careful case analysis for transporting orientations between pseudo-lines in an arrangement. The underlying facts (perspectivity, stretchability of four lines, orientation data of rank-3 oriented matroids) are well established in the oriented-matroid literature. Its only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck independently developing this material around 1981.

'si on ordonne les Δ_i de façon que les u_i aillent en croissant, de même les u'_i]', not 'aillent en [?] ... Cela décrit la croissance, de = les u'_i'.
'Cela décrit la bijection Ω(D) ≃ Ω(D') en termes de la combinatoire de K^1 et de ses ps-droites, sauf dans le cas où il n'y a qu'une seule ps-droite Δ' passant par s et non par t'.
Parenthesis: '(ce qui implique qu'il existe exactement 2 ps.dr. passant par s, i.e. que l'ordre de s est 4, et qu'il existe une [ps.dr.] passant par s et par t)'.
'Supposons qu'il existe une ps.dr. D'' ne passant pas par s, distincte de Δ' (on exclut ici que la figure se réduise à un faisceau de ps.dr. passant par t, et une sécante Δ de ce faisceau)'.
'elle est alors ≠ Δ, Δ', D, D' et ne passe pas par s' rather than 'elle est plane ...'.
'Soient x, x' les pts d'int. de D'' avec D, D' resp., u, u' ceux de Δ avec D, D''.
'on peut comparer par ce qui précède les Ω(D'')...' — 'comparer', not 'compenser'.
